title: Fabric FSDP precision: incorrect dtype during init when using bf16-mixed
author: zhixuan-lin

comments.author: zhixuan-lin
comments.body: Also I think the warning [here](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/pytorch-lightning/blob/8d86b2417d56703d5cc4f0da76acc71717d1dab7/src/lightning/fabric/plugins/precision/fsdp.py#L88-L92) should be probably be for bf16-mixed/fp16-mixed instead of bf16-true/fp16-true, as suggested by the doc https://lightning.ai/docs/fabric/stable/api/fabric_args.html#precision

comments.author: deependujha
comments.body:
hi @zhixuan-lin,

[please refer here](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/fsdp.html#torch.distributed.fsdp.MixedPrecision)

- especially this part:

`param_dtype`: This specifies the dtype for model parameters during forward and backward and thus the dtype for forward and backward computation. **`Outside forward and backward, the sharded parameters are kept in full precision (e.g. for the optimizer step), and for model checkpointing, the parameters are always saved in full precision`**.

---

The warning is emitted, for the reason, when one uses `16-mixed/bf16-mixed`, they are already aware some parameters will be in `full precision`, but when using `16-true or bf16-true`, expectation is no parameters are in `full precision`, which is not the case, so we warn this.

comments.author: zhixuan-lin
comments.body: Hi @deependujha, I understand the warning now, thanks! However, the main problem is that when using bf16-mixed (or bf16-true/fp16-mixed/bf16-mixed), the parameters are initialized to be bf16 instead of fp32. I don't think this is the intended behavior given the doc says `the sharded parameters are kept in full precision`.

comments.author: deependujha
comments.body:
Thanks, we need to update docs. Another thing is, if you keep model weights in torch.Float32, and only buffers and reduce dtype is set to lower precision, there’s little to no improvement.

Is there any specific usecase where you want this?
If so, an option can be to create a new strategy inheriting FSDP and just override the specific method ‘mixed precision config’.

comments.author: zhixuan-lin
comments.body:
I think the standard practice in mixed precision training is to always maintain a main copy of parameters in fp32 and only cast to bf16/fp16 when doing forward/backward (Section 3.1 in [this paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.03740)). For FSDP this reduces both memory consumption and communication costs (sharded parameters are stored in fp32 and when doing gathering for forward/backward we cast to bf16). This is also the semantics of `param_dtype` specified by the official PyTorch doc i.e., `Outside forward and backward, the sharded parameters are kept in full precision`. This explicitly says that the intended behavior is that the parameters themselves should be kept in fp32, even if `param_dtype`is bf16/fp16.

So I think the correct thing to do, at least based on the lightning doc [here](https://lightning.ai/docs/fabric/stable/api/fabric_args.html#precision)  is 
1. For bf16-mixed/fp16-mixed, `module_init_context` should use fp32 
2. For bf16-true/fp16-true, `module_init_context` should use bf16/fp16.

`param_dtype` should always be set to bf16/fp16 though.

comments.author: deependujha
comments.body:
Hi @zhixuan-lin, thanks for your patience and for explaining it clearly. I agree with your proposal.

Would love a PR from you fixing it.
Thanks.
